content.title: Pharmacological Agents for Rate Control in Patients With AF

medications.name: Metoprolol tartrate
medications.dose: 2.5–5 mg bolus over 2 min, up to 3 doses (IV); 25–200 mg, twice daily (Oral)

medications.name: Esmolol
medications.dose: 500 μg/kg bolus over 1 min, then 50–300 μg/kg/min

medications.name: Propranolol
medications.dose: 1 mg over 1 min; repeat as needed every 2 min, up to 3 doses (IV); 10–40 mg, 3–4 times daily (Oral)

medications.name: Diltiazem
medications.dose: 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 min, then repeat, then continuous infusion (IV); 120–360 mg daily (Oral)

medications.name: Verapamil
medications.dose: 5–10 mg IV, then repeat, then continuous infusion (IV); 180–480 mg daily (Oral)

medications.name: Digoxin
medications.dose: 0.25–0.5 mg over several min, 0.0625–0.25 mg daily
medications.note: Renally eliminated, increased mortality at plasma concentrations >1.2 ng/mL

medications.name: Amiodarone
medications.dose: 150–300 mg IV, then 10–50 mg/h (IV); 100–200 mg daily (Oral)

recommendations_for_acute_rate_control.recommendation: Patients with AF and rapid ventricular response who are hemodynamically stable should use beta blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers.
For those where beta blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are ineffective, digoxin may be used.
In cases of rapid ventricular response, adding intravenous magnesium may be beneficial.
Intravenous amiodarone is advisable for critical instability or decompensated heart failure.
Avoid nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in severe left ventricular dysfunction.
